64:T12c8,## Problem

The agent-scope re-key migration (`eliza-workflow-agent-scope-v1`) quarantines pre-existing workflow rows under the `__legacy_unscoped__` sentinel tenant. The `TRIGGER_DISPATCH` tasks those workflows already armed remain owned by the live agent.

Those durable tasks continue firing. Tenant-scoped workflow lookup returns `Workflow not found`, and the trigger runtime persists a high-priority **Automation failed** notification on every due interval.

## Root cause

Workflow rows are authoritative; scheduler tasks are derived state. Startup rehydration only recreated tasks for active workflows. It never reconciled workflow-derived tasks that no longer resolved to an active workflow in the current tenant, and its optional runtime-method guards could silently declare startup healthy while stale tasks remained armed.

## Fix

- Reconcile every agent-scoped, workflow-kind task against the tenant's active workflow IDs before valid schedules are re-armed.
- Delete tasks for missing, inactive, or malformed workflow references. A workflow task without a persistent ID is a fatal invariant violation.
- Treat `rehydrateSchedules()` as the startup error boundary: wrap failures in `ElizaError`, report `WORKFLOW_SCHEDULE_RECONCILIATION_FAILED` through `runtime.reportError`, and fail startup.
- Remove optional capability probes around required `IAgentRuntime` task APIs. A runtime without the persistent scheduler contract is not ready.
- Keep the query agent-scoped, so another agent sharing the same database is untouched.

## Persistent integration proof

`orphaned-schedule-reconciliation.test.ts` uses the real `PgliteDatabaseAdapter`, SQL migrations, two real `AgentRuntime` tenants, the real workflow tables, real core task table, real `TaskService` + trigger worker, real workflow dispatch, and real `NotificationService`. There is no fake task array.

The test proves the failure before proving the repair:

1. Tenant A owns one valid schedule and one schedule whose workflow row is moved to `__legacy_unscoped__`; tenant B owns a valid schedule in the same physical database.
2. The orphan is made due and fired through the real scheduler. Observed backend path:
   - `Workflow execution failed for orphaned-tenant-a-workflow: Workflow not found: orphaned-tenant-a-workflow`
   - a real high-priority workflow failure notification is persisted.
3. PGlite is closed and reopened from the same data directory (process-restart boundary).
4. Startup logs `Removed 1 orphaned workflow schedule task(s) whose workflow is no longer active in this tenant`.
5. After restart:
   - tenant A's orphan task is absent;
   - tenant A's valid schedule is present;
   - tenant B's valid task retains the exact pre-restart ID;
   - the quarantined workflow row remains as the migration artifact;
   - a real scheduler tick creates no execution and does not replace/increment the persisted failure notification.

65:T131f,## Why

Cloud chat still feels 2-3s. Measured the DB geometry + per-turn round-trips:

**Geometry (measured 2026-07-23):**
- Railway PG origin: us-west (Railway proxy `switchback.proxy.rlwy.net`, SF/us-west region, PG 18.4)
- Worker: Cloudflare (staging worker placement seen at ORD; prod has smart placement)
- Per-query RTT from a cross-region client on an ESTABLISHED connection: **~162ms** (10x `SELECT 1`, 162-179ms). Worker(ORD)->Hyperdrive->Railway(us-west) per-query RTT is the same order: every serial DB round-trip on the turn path costs real wall-clock.

**Per-turn DB timeline for a shared-tier SSE chat turn (the PWA hot path):**

| # | Query | Serial/parallel | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | scope resolve (auth+org+agent) | serial | pre-turn (KV scope cache #COLDPATH already absorbs warm case) |
| 2 | `findRunningSandbox` | serial | bridgeStream |
| 3 | character lookup + history read | **parallel** (Promise.all) | pre-model |
| 4 | `reserveCredits` (atomic CTE: FOR UPDATE + insert) | serial | pre-model |
| 5 | model inference (Cerebras) | — | ~1-2.5s |
| 6 | history upsert | serial | post-last-token |
| 7 | `billUsage` -> calculateCost (pricing read, in-memory cached) | serial | **was inline before `done`** |
| 8 | `reservation.reconcile` (settlement lookup + UPDATE + refund txn, in a write txn) | serial | **was inline before `done`** |
| 9 | `recordUsageAnalytics` (usage_records insert, staging mean 4.6ms exec + RTT) | serial | **was inline before `done`** |
| 10 | `aiBillingRecords.record` (audit insert) | serial | **was inline before `done`** |

Steps 7-10 are ~4+ serial cross-region round-trips ≈ **1.5-2s of pure RTT after the reply text is already final**. That matches the staging measurement (CHAT-LATENCY-MEASURE-2026-07-22): firstText ~1.4-1.7s but `done` ~4-4.8s.

The **non-stream** send already fixed this exact shape with `settleOffResponsePath` + `executionCtx.waitUntil` (#8759 pattern; see the existing deferred-billing tests). The SSE stream path — which is what the PWA actually uses — never got it.

## What

- `bridgeSharedMessageStream` / `bridgeStream` accept an optional `BridgeExecutionContext`; the billing tail (billUsage -> settle -> analytics -> audit) runs via `settleOffResponsePath`: deferred through `waitUntil` on a Worker, inline (byte-identical behavior) without one.
- `canonical-scoped-stream` threads an optional `executionCtx` to `bridgeStream` (voice + REST SSE both route through it).
- Both HTTP SSE routes pass their Worker executionCtx with the same throw-safe degrade the non-stream route uses.

## Money invariants (tested against the REAL `bridgeSharedMessageStream`)

- `done` frame flushes while billUsage is still in flight; the deferred task settles the hold at `billing.totalCost`.
- A billUsage throw refunds the hold (idempotent `reconcile(0)`), contained so waitUntil never sees an unhandled rejection.
- No executionCtx -> tail runs inline, settled by the time the stream drains (pre-deferral behavior for tests/non-Worker callers).
- Nav-intent turns still refund synchronously, never touch waitUntil.
- `sweep-credit-reservations` cron remains the backstop for a dropped waitUntil.

## Expected impact

~1.5-2s off every shared-tier chat turn's `done` latency. First-token timing unchanged; the socket now closes when the reply does instead of after the billing writes.

66:T18f2,Fixes #17034

## Root cause

#16983's `tryGateEvaluator` requires "the planner did not explicitly declare the turn incomplete" before synthesizing a FINISH from a terminal action result — but on the native function-calling lane `parsePlannerOutput` returns `raw = { text, toolCalls }` only, so the planner had **no channel** to declare that. The veto was structurally inert on exactly the lane the action-owned `turnComplete` gate targets: a multi-op request whose native model emits calls sequentially (one planner round at a time, instead of a parallel batch) would satisfy every gate precondition after op 1 and end the turn with a truthful-but-partial reply, silently dropping the remaining operations.

## Architecture

Turn scope is planner-owned, pre-execution knowledge — sound to collect before dispatch, unlike result certification (which #16889's triage correctly rejected as pre-dispatch prose and which stays action-owned via `turnComplete`). This change gives the native planner a structured turn-scope channel and folds it into the existing veto:

- Every native tool schema gains a reserved optional enum argument `eliza_turn_scope` (`"final" | "more_work_pending"`), injected non-mutatingly by `withTurnScopeToolArg` at the single `callPlanner` seam. Schemas that are not object-shaped, or that already declare the reserved name, are left untouched; `required` is never extended.
- `parsePlannerOutput` folds per-call declarations into a first-class `completed` field — any `more_work_pending` in a batch wins, otherwise a positive `final` is captured, unknown values strip silently with no opinion — and **strips the argument before dispatch**, so no action handler, arg validator, or clipboard projection ever sees it. The JSON lane's explicit top-level `completed` boolean outranks per-call scope args.
- The loop consumes the folded signal where it previously probed `raw.completed`; `tryGateEvaluator` itself is unchanged — precondition 6 (`completed !== false`) now simply functions on the native lane.
- Absence preserves pre-change behavior exactly: no scope arg → no opinion → gate eligibility identical to #16983. Only an explicit `more_work_pending` vetoes, mirroring the JSON lane where only `completed: false` blocks.
- One prompt rule added to `plannerTemplate` teaching the reserved argument (single lane-neutral sentence; the JSON lane's `completed` rule is unchanged).

## Tests

10 new tests (`packages/core/src/runtime/__tests__/planner-loop.test.ts`), all deterministic:

- **The #17034 canonical regression**: a native sequential multi-op turn — round 1 declares `more_work_pending`, the action's `turnComplete` cannot end the turn, the evaluator continues, round 2 executes the second op, the evaluator owns the combined final reply. Two executions, two evaluations, no truncation.
- Native single-call veto (`more_work_pending` + terminal action result → evaluator runs) with strip assertion on the dispatched params.
- Native `final` scope alongside a terminal action result → gate still fires, dispatch stripped.
- Parse-level: derive `completed` false/true, unknown-value no-opinion strip, pending-outvotes-final in a batch, JSON-lane top-level `completed` outranks per-call args.
- Injection: object schemas gain the optional enum without mutating the originals or touching `required`; schema-less/non-object tools returned by reference; a genuine parameter already using the reserved name is never overwritten.

Full suite on the rebased head: planner-loop 110/110; all core runtime suites + message executor context **993/993**; `tsc --noEmit` clean for `@elizaos/core`; Biome clean on the three changed files.

- This proves the fast path is unregressed live with the new schema+prompt in place. The veto path (model volunteering `more_work_pending`) is inherently nondeterministic to force live and is pinned by the deterministic loop-level regressions above.

## What changed

- Tracks detached post-delivery tasks and drains them before normal runtime shutdown, preventing evaluator/database work from racing teardown.
- Adds `backgroundQuiescenceMs` and `totalToQuiescenceMs` to the live Cerebras report.
- Skips semantic reflection for stateless simple replies; durable user information, URLs, action results, and non-REPLY behavior still evaluate.
- Coalesces reflection context preparation per message so fact, relationship, identity, and success evaluators share message/entity/relationship reads.
- Defers secret access/audit writes under Cloudflare `waitUntil`, caches decrypted pooled credentials for 60 seconds with invalidation on org changes or provider auth failures, and extends the invalidation-driven pool snapshot lifetime.
- Combines pooled daily usage and `last_used_at` into one atomic SQL round trip.
- Removes the PR evidence-row gate, the polling Develop PR aggregate, its bespoke state-machine tests, and the standalone stale-base PR workflow. Ordinary lint, format, typecheck, build, cloud tests, title validation, and security checks remain.

## Root causes

`handleMessage` returned after connector delivery while an untracked post-turn task launched another live model call and 20+ adapter operations. The benchmark called this state final, then shut down the database while work was still active. That detached work also overlapped later turns, inflating provider and message-service tails.

Cloud pooled credential selection independently decrypted the same secret and awaited access/audit writes before every inference request.

The two reviewed latency PRs were closed unmerged. #16882's proposed 3-second provider timeout is absent from current `develop`; provider composition uses parallel execution, in-flight coalescing, cache reuse, and the turn cancellation signal without a blanket compose timeout. #16820's 1.5-second browser latency threshold is also absent.

Replaces the placeholder live gate in `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/sensitive-request-hosted-page-e2e.test.ts` — which unconditionally threw `"live sensitive-request round-trip harness not run in CI"` so supplying the documented credentials could never turn the leg green — with a **real, fail-closed live harness** that drives the hosted-secret round-trip against the **real deployed cloud** (`elizacloud.ai`), plus a credential-gated real-Telegram connector leg for the owner run.

When `ELIZA_SENSITIVE_LIVE=1` + `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY` are set the harness executes, with zero stand-ins:

- **create** over the real `POST /api/v1/sensitive-requests` (API-key actor → real Postgres row, `sr_` single-use token mint)
- **hosted page shell** — real `GET /sensitive-requests/:id` serves the deployed HTML page
- **token-gated public view** — `GET /api/v1/sensitive-requests/:id?token=` (pending form spec, no audit exposure to token holders)
- **sessionless single-use-token submit** of a random sentinel → `fulfilled`, a **real org-secret row** created (`secret.set` audit carries the `secretId`)
- **replay** of the consumed token → **409**; **tampered token** → **401** on both view and submit *without* burning the genuine token; canceled request → late submit **409**
- **agent-side observation** per the production contract: the org-credentialed private view (what an agent container holds) shows `pending → fulfilled` + the full audit sequence
- **no-secret-on-the-wire sweep**: every response body captured during the run is asserted to never contain the submitted value

Two real-behavior discoveries are encoded in the harness: org secret names are unique and there is **no secret-delete API**, so each run mints a fresh timestamped target key (a repeat run previously 500'd on `secretsService.create` duplicate); and the submit route's STRICT rate limit can 429 back-to-back runs, so 429s are waited out (`Retry-After`) rather than misread as flow outcomes.

The connector-DM leg (additionally gated on `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` + `ELIZA_SENSITIVE_LIVE_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`) sends the **real Telegram Bot API DM** in the exact wire shape the production Telegraf adapter emits (text + one inline `Provide securely` URL button, never any secret material), then **fail-closed polls** the request until the human taps and submits on the hosted page — no submit within the window fails the test.

CI behavior is unchanged: without the env the live tests skip with a reason; the nine deterministic cases still run.

# Risks

Notification `data.previousTotalUsd`/`currentTotalUsd` on a flip tick now carry the residual totals the materiality decision was made on (internally consistent with `deltaUsd`/`deltaPct`).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Fixes two confirmed failure modes in the merged #17039 coverage-flip re-baseline path:

- **Failure A (attacker-timed mute).** A dexscreener price listing appearing on a spam token (fake liquidity) on the SAME tick as a real crash in priced holdings read as a coverage flip and re-baselined the whole total — the crash notification was swallowed, falsifying the #17039 PR-body invariant that a spam airdrop can never mute a concurrent material move.
- **Failure B (permanent mute via flap).** A coverage bit flapping priced↔unpriced on one dust position re-baselined the whole total EVERY tick, so slow material drift on the honestly-priced holdings never accumulated — the watcher was permanently muted, with no signal above debug.

The fix records per-position USD values in the baseline alongside the coverage bits (same key set, validator-enforced congruence). On a flip, the comparison excises ONLY the flipped positions from both totals:

- a material move in the residual (consistently-priced) holdings still notifies;
- an immaterial residual re-baselines just the flipped contribution, so the anchor keeps accumulating drift;
- three consecutive silent flip re-baselines escalate via `runtime.reportError("WalletBalanceDelta.coverageFlap", …)` → `RECENT_ERRORS`, so a flapping feed is a visible systemic problem instead of a silent debug loop.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking; cache-row schema migrates by designed discard).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation. The module header prose documents the new residual-comparison and flap-escalation invariants.

6b:T98b,## Problem
Every fleet-upgrade (agent_upgrade) job on staging failed for 48h+ with:
`Blue provision failed: Headscale routing is required, but the sandbox did not register a headscale_ip.`
This left the whole staging agent fleet pinned to stale images (some from Jul 9/18) while the platform kept deploying — Shadow's demo QA hit pre-16836 settings-auth errors and double-message bugs on a *brand new* signup because the container image predated the fixes.

## Root cause (verified live on staging)
During blue/green upgrade the preserved GREEN node holds the base hostname (`eliza-<agentId>`). When the BLUE container's tailscaled registers the same hostname, **Headscale collision-renames it** to `<name>-<random>` (observed: `eliza-00e6292c-e55-cnpx9uop` registered at 08:22:44Z). `waitForRegistration` polls `getNodeByName` with an **exact** name match, never sees the suffixed node, and times out after 180s — while blue is healthy and registered the whole time.

## Fix
- `HeadscaleClient.getNodeByNameOrSuffixed(name, {excludeNodeId})`: matches `name` OR `name-*`, excluding the preserved green node id; exact match wins, otherwise newest suffixed registration.
- `waitForRegistration` uses it (still honors `excludeNodeId` per #16565 so it can never adopt green's IP).

## Receipts
- Live repro + verification in staging worker logs (08:19-08:24Z): image pulled, container created+healthy, tailscaled registered with suffixed name, worker timed out polling exact name.
- 15/15 agent_upgrade failures in 48h with identical error before this.

6c:T118a,## Problem

`normalizeSchemaForCerebras` stripped `properties`, `required`, and
`additionalProperties` from empty object schemas, producing a bare
`{"type":"object"}`. Cerebras rejects that shape while compiling the complete
tool grammar, so one no-argument tool can fail an otherwise valid planner
request with HTTP 400.

The review also found a second failure mode: populated object schemas reached
through keywords such as `prefixItems` were walked but left open. Cerebras
strict mode requires `additionalProperties: false` on every object in the
schema, not only empty objects.

## Fix

- Represent strict no-argument tools as
  `{"type":"object","properties":{},"additionalProperties":false}`.
- Close every strict object schema at every supported schema-bearing depth,
  including populated tuple objects.
- Infer `type: "object"` when object-only keywords describe an implicit object.
- Preserve non-strict open-map semantics instead of replacing a schema-valued
  `additionalProperties`.
- Keep illegal non-object tool roots beneath the existing closed `value`
  wrapper and clone visited nodes rather than mutating caller-owned schemas.
- Pass each tool's strictness from `plugin-openai` into the core normalizer.

This matches Cerebras's documented strict-tool requirement that
`additionalProperties` be explicitly false for every object:
https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/capabilities/tool-use

## Live provider validation

The live test sends three strict tools through the real plugin and Cerebras
`gpt-oss-120b`:

1. a no-argument `IGNORE` tool;
2. a forced `RECORD_EVIDENCE` tool;
3. a tuple tool containing a populated object under `prefixItems`.

The captured request proves both formerly invalid object shapes reach the wire
with `additionalProperties: false`. Cerebras returned HTTP 200 and a real
`RECORD_EVIDENCE` call with `{"verdict":"verified","count":2}`.

6d:T12b8,Follow-up hardening for #17066 (merged mid-review as `7cd6e85aeba`), closing both load-bearing gaps @NubsCarson's adversarial review found — one of which was a factual error in the merged PR's own security argument. Both were verified against the code before fixing.

## 1. The pool boot key was NOT revoked at claim (merged premise factually wrong)

The pool container's inference key is minted during `provision(poolRowId, WARM_POOL_ORG_ID)`, so its name is `agent-sandbox:<poolRowId>`. The claim transaction UPDATEs the **user's** row and DELETEs the pool row — so the claim-time mint (`createForAgent({agentSandboxId: claimedRow.id})`) revokes `agent-sandbox:<userAgentId>`, a **different name**, and the pool-org key survived every claim as an active credential bound to a row that no longer existed. The merged doc comments described a revoke no caller performed ("same sandbox id ⇒ same name"; "the caller drives `apiKeysService.revokeForAgent` against the pool org").

Fix:
- `claimWarmContainer` returns the claimed row augmented with `warm_pool_row_id` (typed `WarmClaimedAgentSandbox`) — the deleted pool row's id exists nowhere else once the transaction commits, and the boot key's name derives from it.
- `pushClaimedWarmContainerInferenceKey` revokes `agent-sandbox:<poolRowId>` **after a successful push** — never on the push-failure branch (the container's gateway relay may still be signing with that key) and never on a fingerprint mismatch. Best-effort teardown (`error-policy:J6`): a revoke failure emits the stable `warm_pool.pool_key_revoke_failed` event instead of failing the claim.
- The false doc comments are corrected to the real mechanics.

## 2. `pushed: true` attested transport acceptance, not an applied swap

`POST /api/cloud/login/persist` now echoes `appliedKeyFingerprint` — a 16-hex sha-256 prefix of the cloud key the runtime **resolves after the swap**, probed via `runtime.getSetting` (the same precedence chain inference uses, so a stale key shadowing via character secrets is *detected*, not papered over), with `process.env` as fallback. The pusher compares it against the key it minted:

- match → `verified: true` (process-verified swap; claim logs carry it);
- mismatch → throws (caller emits `warm_pool.key_push_failed`) and the pool-key revoke is skipped — the container is never stripped of the only credential it may still hold while the swap demonstrably didn't take;
- absent (older container image predating the echo) → `pushed: true, verified: false` — the push stands, flagged unverified, so image version skew cannot fail claims.

Only digest prefixes cross the wire, never key material; the no-secret-in-logs pins cover the fingerprint path too. On the push-failure branch nothing schedules a container restart (no restart primitive exists in the sandbox service today) — the row env carries the new key so the next restart self-heals, and the stable failure event is the operator hook; this is documented in the method contract rather than papered over.

The deleted `setTtsDebugSink` export had zero callers repo-wide.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Server-side `ELIZA_TTS_DEBUG` was a dead diagnostic: `ttsDebug` in `@elizaos/shared` only emitted through a sink installed via `setTtsDebugSink()`, and no production code ever called it. Booting any server with `ELIZA_TTS_DEBUG=1` produced zero `[tts]` lines while the cloud TTS proxy's call sites traced into the void — operators believed tracing was on and got silence.

Per the error-handling doctrine (no half-alive diagnostics), this wires the real thing instead of deleting the flag:

- **`packages/shared/src/utils/tts-debug.ts`** — `ttsDebug` now emits straight through the structured logger (`logger.info(detail, "[eliza][tts] <phase>")`) whenever the flag is set. No per-host sink wiring exists to forget: the bare agent server, the app-core API, and the packaged desktop all trace from the same module. The dead `setTtsDebugSink` API is removed. Info level is deliberate: the operator opted in explicitly, so lines must be visible at the default `LOG_LEVEL` rather than hiding behind `debug`.
- **`plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/routes/local-inference-tts-route.ts`** — the local TTS path (`POST /api/tts/local-inference`) now traces `server:local-tts:request|success|reject` phases, mirroring the cloud proxy's `server:cloud-tts:*`, so both server TTS paths are observable under the flag.
- **`plugins/plugin-elizacloud/src/lib/tts-debug.ts`** — header updated to describe the real mechanism.

The renderer flavor (`packages/ui/src/utils/tts-debug.ts`, Vite define) already worked and is untouched.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking; dead diagnostic made real).

# Documentation changes needed?

None beyond the file headers updated in this diff — `packages/shared/src/utils/tts-debug.ts` is itself the documentation of the flag and now describes the actual mechanism and both server phase families.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`packages/shared/src/utils/tts-debug.ts` (the 3-line emission core), then the live server logs in Evidence Details — a real bare-agent boot with the flag on shows the full `server:cloud-tts:*` trace against the real Eliza Cloud upstream, and a second boot with the flag off shows zero lines for the same requests.

## Detailed testing steps

Emission is asserted on the structured logger's **real** listener stream (`addLogListener`), driven through the real route handlers — no logger mocks:

- `packages/shared/src/utils/tts-debug.test.ts` (new): flag-off silence, falsy/truthy flag variants (`0/false/off/no` vs `1/true/yes/on`), info-level entry carrying phase + detail, phase-only entries, preview collapsing/truncation.
- `plugins/plugin-elizacloud/src/lib/server-cloud-tts.test.ts`: successful proxy emits `proxy → upstream-ok → success` with the client correlation header (`x-elizaos-tts-message-id`) and spoken-text preview riding along; missing cloud key emits `reject (no_api_key)`; the same successful request with the flag unset emits **zero** tts lines.
- `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/routes/local-inference-tts-route.test.ts`: `request`+`success` on synthesis (incl. voice hint), `reject (synthesis_failed)` carrying the error message, `reject (runtime_unavailable)`, and flag-off silence.

The repo test setup pins `LOG_LEVEL=error`, which would gate info-level lines off before the listener sees them; the three suites use `vi.hoisted` to set `LOG_LEVEL=info` before the logger module initializes (the production default this diagnostic is documented against).

Full suites at the branch head: `packages/shared` **1293 passed** (114 files), `plugin-elizacloud` **390 passed** (47 files), `plugin-local-inference` **2607 passed** (253 files). Root `bun run verify` exit 0.

Low-to-medium. This changes only late plugin registration on an already initialized runtime. A schema-bearing plugin now waits for its own DDL before publication/service start. Migrations are serialized per adapter, concurrent registration of the same plugin joins one in-flight migration, and any migration failure still rejects registration before components are published. Initial boot behavior while an adapter reports not-ready is unchanged.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Moves late-plugin schema migration ahead of base plugin registration, which is the point that eagerly initializes services.
- Sends only the incoming plugin's real schema to the adapter instead of re-running every registered plugin migration.
- Serializes migration work per adapter and deduplicates simultaneous registrations of the same plugin name.
- Preserves fail-closed rollback and propagates readiness/migration failures.
- Adds a real isolated PGlite regression using the actual inbox plugin, actual `RuntimeMigrator`, and actual `InboxMigrationService`.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking).

# Documentation changes needed?

No. This repairs an internal lifecycle ordering invariant and adds executable regression coverage; no public API or operator workflow changes.

# Risks

Low. The change is limited to the Smithers subprocess payload/error lifecycle and
its regression coverage. The successful workflow path, dedicated FD 3 transport,
restricted child environment, timeout, abort handling, and worker protocol remain
unchanged. Failure text is now bounded, VT-stripped, and secret-redacted before it
enters the typed error.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

The Smithers launcher previously called `child.stdio[3].end(payload)` before that
stream had an `error` observer. If the worker closed FD 3 early, Node emitted an
unhandled `EPIPE` and crashed the host process instead of returning an observable
workflow failure. This is the exact failure captured in the real Docker CI job:
[run 29954836153 / job 89041403450](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29954836153/job/89041403450).

This PR:

- observes stdout, stderr, process exit, timeout, abort, and FD 3 before writing;
- awaits payload delivery instead of letting a later stream event escape;
- converts spawn, payload, and worker failures into `ElizaError` with code
  `SMITHERS_WORKFLOW_FAILED`, a preserved cause, phase, and exit code;
- bounds and sanitizes worker stderr before exposing it; and
- adds a real Node child regression that closes FD 3, emits more than 8 KiB of
  stderr containing a fake secret, and exits 42.

The separate workflow-inbox migration race is deliberately excluded from this
narrow repair.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking).

# Documentation changes needed?

No user-facing documentation change is needed. This repairs an internal subprocess
failure boundary and includes executable regression coverage.

72:T1967,Fixes #16889

## Root cause

Native function-calling does not carry a trustworthy post-action `messageToUser`. Adding anticipatory planner prose, as originally proposed, would let text produced before dispatch falsely certify that the action succeeded and that the turn is complete. The existing `continueChain` flag cannot serve as that certificate either: it is a legacy immediate chain-abort signal, so using it for evaluator gating can truncate a queued batch.

## Architecture

This change adds an explicit, provider-independent `turnComplete` result contract owned by the action:

- `true` makes the result eligible for terminal gating; `false` vetoes gating; absent delegates to normal evaluation.
- Eligibility additionally requires exactly one executed tool in the turn, a successful latest result, a drained planned queue, no accumulated failure, planner completion not explicitly false, and non-empty canonical `userFacingText` marked `verifiedUserFacing`.
- Multi-tool batches are counted across active and archived planner steps, so the last tool cannot accidentally become terminal merely because the queue just drained.
- Failed, partial, ambiguous, unsafe, missing-output, queued, and explicitly incomplete turns retain the model-backed evaluator.
- The existing text/XML planner-owned gate and `continueChain` behavior remain intact.
- Gated trajectories record `action_terminal_result` with `llmCallSkipped: true` and no model attribution.

`SETTINGS` opts in only for successful list/set operations whose returned text describes the actual completed result. Its GET/capability-description path and every failure remain evaluator-backed.

# Risks

Low. Four finding-scoped fixes: a strictly narrower response-handler evaluator trigger (only assertions fire; every previously-caught fabrication shape is regression-locked), a SQL-side subject filter that tightens a read the evening BRIEF consumes, an env-precedence flip in the scenario-runner judge transport, and an error-policy annotation + `runtime.reportError` on an existing designed degrade. No schema changes, no new runtime surfaces.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

### P1 — `core.simple_completed_side_effect_claim` false-positived on consent-seeking offers (`packages/core/src/services/message.ts`)

The merged claim pattern made the completion auxiliary optional (`i(?:['’]ve| have| just)?\s+set…`), so the bare `I`+verb branch matched consent-seeking and conditional phrasings. Verified against the merged regex on this branch: **"Should I set a reminder for tomorrow?", "Shall I set…", "Before I set…, what time works?", "If I set…, would that work?", "When I set reminders… should I?" all matched** — each would be rewritten to "On it." and rerouted to the planner: the user asks a question and receives an action they did not consent to. Detection is now split by grammatical certainty, and only ASSERTIONS of a completed side effect fire (the zero-tools gate was already in `shouldRun`: RESPOND + `requiresTool !== true` + simple-context-only turns):

- **Perfective claims** ("I've set…", "I have scheduled…", "I just added…") keep matching in any sentence shape — including tag questions ("I've set two reminders — anything else?") — unless led by a subordinator ("Once I've set…").
- **Bare simple-past claims** ("I set a reminder for the 28th at 9am.") fire only when the word before "I" is not a modal/interrogative/subordinator AND the containing sentence does not end in "?".
- **State claims** ("that's all set", "reminders are set", "Done —") are unchanged, including develop's sentence-start anchor on "done —".
- All offer/question/conditional shapes above plus "Want me to set…?", "Do you want me to set…?", "Would you like me to add…?", "I could set… if you like", "Once I've set…, I'll confirm" pass through; "Done — I have set two reminders." and the bare-past report are still caught.

### P2 — completed-today read applied LIMIT 24 before the owner filter (`plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/lifeops/{repository,service}.ts`)

`listCompletedOccurrenceViewsSince` applied `LIMIT 24` in SQL while `listOwnerOccurrencesCompletedToday` filtered `subjectType === "owner"` in TypeScript. Under multi-room load, newer agent-subject completions consume the window and owner wins silently drop out of the evening BRIEF — a broken pipeline reading as a win-less day. The subject filter now lives in the SQL `WHERE` ahead of the `LIMIT` (options object `{ subjectType, limit }`), the service scans with `{ subjectType: "owner", limit: 200 }` sized for its 36h lookback (newest-first, so the local-day filter only trims the older tail), and the 24-item display cap is applied last.

### P2 — CerebrasJudge key precedence inverted (`packages/scenario-runner/src/cerebras-judge.ts`)

The constructor read `CEREBRAS_API_KEY ?? EVAL_CEREBRAS_API_KEY` — inverted vs the eval-model resolution order everywhere else (role-specific `EVAL_` first; `CEREBRAS_API_KEY` doubles as the live-provider selector for the model under test in `live-provider.ts`). On a host carrying both, the under-test credential silently took over judging. Flipped: `options.apiKey ?? EVAL_CEREBRAS_API_KEY ?? CEREBRAS_API_KEY`.

### P2 — `loadCompletedTodayFromService` catch fabricated an empty wins list (`plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/actions/brief.ts`)

The catch degraded with a log-only `logger.warn` and returned `[]` with no error-policy annotation — a broken load silently implied a win-less day. The degrade is kept as designed (the brief composes from independent optional sources; one broken source must not kill the whole evening brief, and the wins section is omitted rather than rendered healthy-empty), now annotated `// error-policy:J4` and surfaced through `runtime.reportError("Brief.loadCompletedToday", error, { surface: "evening-brief-wins" })` so RECENT_ERRORS and owner escalation observe the failure.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fixes (non-breaking) + error-policy doctrine compliance + regression tests.

None — rationale comments live at the fix sites per the comment doctrine.

## Known gaps / failures

**The forced no-tools synthesis warn (`[planner-loop] tool work finished without a usable reply; forced a no-tools synthesis pass`) did not fire in any live run on this branch — 17 recorded live turns across claude-opus-4-8, claude-haiku-4-5, claude-opus-4-7, and the claude-sdk backend.** The trigger requires a finished tool turn whose final message is empty/unsafe WITHOUT a deliberate STOP/IGNORE; the current subscription CLI models never enter that state:

- natural save/read/list/history turns (6 turns, 3 models): every finished tool turn carried a usable grounded reply;
- "reply with exactly `tool calls`" / markup-narration demands (3 turns): the model refused to emit markup-shaped final messages ("I can't dress this up as a system trace or name internal functions") or Stage-1 routed the turn simple;
- "no response needed" / "send an empty reply" demands (3 turns): the model either replied anyway or chose an explicit `IGNORE` terminal — which is the deliberate-silence exemption, live-verified above as correctly NOT synthesizing;
- leading/trailing invocation-literal demands `call:DONE{ok}` (3 turns, both backends): the model appended the literal after prose (kept usable by design — the heuristic is start-anchored) or refused to lead with it ("I can't lead a message with an injected control string");
- six-item batch save (1 turn): partial save + clarifying reply; recap turns (opus-4-8/haiku/opus-4-7) routed to a simple REPLY at Stage-1 (see observation below).

The firing behavior itself is pinned deterministically: `planner-loop.test.ts` "tool-turn reply guarantee (#16935)" drives the REAL `runPlannerLoop` post-pass (scripted model outputs are the only way to force a replyless finish on demand — which is precisely what the 17 recorded live attempts demonstrate): it asserts the ONE extra no-tools call happens, its grounded prose ships, deliberate IGNORE is exempt, and a synthesis failure keeps the original result — 110/110 green on this branch. The originally recorded live firing (#16966 PR body, `synthesizedUsable=false`, iteration=2) remains the only live capture of the line; on current models the net is provably (17/17) not being hit. I could not produce an honest live firing without mocking the model mid-loop, which would not be live evidence.

74:T1414,Closes #17035. Supersedes #17009 and #16981.

## Summary

- separate internal dashboard relays from planner-visible message connectors
- route each swarm synthesis through its originating connector, falling back to
  the dashboard only when no origin is available
- remove the normalized-text/time-window delivery guard; independent identical
  replies are preserved instead of guessed to be duplicates
- add real-`AgentRuntime` coverage proving a dashboard-origin swarm result
  produces one memory and one WebSocket event

This fixes transport ownership at the producers. It does not normalize,
compare, delay, hide, or suppress assistant text.

## Root causes and triggering conditions

There were two distinct producer-side fan-outs.

### Synchronous dashboard turn: SSE plus WebSocket

The streaming conversation route owns the immediate reply over SSE.
`client_chat` is separately an internal relay that persists a message and emits
`proactive-message` over WebSocket.

`AgentRuntime.registerSendHandler` previously both installed a callable handler
and advertised its source through `getMessageConnectors()`. Registering
`client_chat` that way made the dashboard relay selectable by the planner's
`MESSAGE op=send` path. A duplicate occurred when:

1. a turn used the streaming dashboard route;
2. the dashboard relay handlers were registered;
3. the planner selected `client_chat` for the same synchronous turn; and
4. the UI received both the route-owned SSE reply and relay-owned WebSocket
   event.

The two startup `connectWs()` calls do not construct two live sockets:
`ElizaClient.connectWs()` returns while its socket is `CONNECTING` or `OPEN`.
That symptom is two transports, not two WebSocket connections.

### Swarm synthesis: two WebSocket producers

`handleSwarmSynthesis` unconditionally called both:

1. `routeMessage(..., "swarm_synthesis")`, which broadcasts through the
   dashboard autonomy relay; and
2. `routeSynthesisToConnector(...)`, which resolves the originating room and
   sends through its handler.

For a dashboard-origin room, the second branch resolves to `client_chat`, so
both branches broadcast `proactive-message` for one synthesis. For an external
origin, the same result was sent to both the external connector and dashboard.

Synthesis now has one owner: the exact origin transport. The dashboard relay is
only used when no origin exists. Origin transport failures propagate instead of
invoking a second sender after an uncertain partial delivery.

## Why text dedupe was removed

The merged `delivery-dedupe` guard lowercased and normalized message content,
then suppressed matching text in the same room for two seconds. It could drop
legitimate repeated replies such as two independent `done` events, while not
preventing the ephemeral swarm fan-out it was intended to cover.

Stable request/event IDs remain the right mechanism for retry idempotency. Text
equality is not delivery identity.

## Related-PR audit

I scanned every currently open PR patch for message-content/time-window
suppression and duplicate-reply work. No other open PR implements this smell.
The related proposals are #17009 and #16981; both are closed and unmerged.
Open PRs involving structural operation IDs, tool-call IDs, canary targets, or
presence fingerprints address different identity domains and are not replaced
by this change.

77:T1979,Fixes #16843

## Summary

- keep a Capacitor renderer connected over REST/SSE when its remote agent base would derive an insecure `ws://` URL
- preserve the existing WebSocket behavior for normal HTTP pages and for secure `wss://` targets
- prove the fallback with boundary tests plus a real ephemeral TCP HTTP/SSE integration server

## Root cause

The iOS remote-connect smoke runs the packaged WebView at `capacitor://localhost` against a healthy loopback agent at `http://127.0.0.1:31338`. REST health succeeds through the native HTTP path, but the client still tried `ws://127.0.0.1:31338/ws`. The socket never opened, so the UI stayed `disconnected` until the smoke timed out despite the backend being healthy.

The existing HTTPS mixed-content fallback already models this transport correctly: REST/SSE is authoritative and the shell reports connected without opening the unusable cleartext socket. This patch applies that exact policy to the Capacitor renderer protocol only.

## Compatibility boundaries

- `capacitor:` renderer + `http:` agent → REST-only, no WebSocket construction
- `http:` renderer + `http:` agent → unchanged `ws://` connection
- `capacitor:` renderer + `https:` agent → unchanged `wss://` connection
- shared-runtime, dedicated Cloud, local IPC, and iOS in-process rules are unchanged

78:T190e,## Problem

Expanding the home notification shade set the apps region to `h-0 opacity-0` + `inert`: every app vanished from the home, focus had to be teleported into the shade and back, and a short inbox left ~40% (mobile) to ~60% (desktop) of the screen as dead black space. Reported as: *"expanding notifications hides apps. It's weird."*

## Change

The home column is now **one vertical scroller** (iOS-lock-screen model — "push, don't hide"):

- `HomeScreen`: the content column owns vertical scroll; the shade and apps are content-sized siblings. The `appsDisplaced` / `inert` / displaced-focus machinery is **deleted** (~90 lines). The column is passed to the shade as `pageSurfaceRef`, which also wires up the background pull lanes the real home never enabled (`emptyGestureTargetRef` was never passed).
- `NotificationsHomeCenter`: the expanded list is content-height — no internal scroll, no height cap. All directional gestures (touch pull, mouse drag, wheel accumulator) now gate on the **page** scroller: expand only at the page top; push-to-close only where the push cannot mean scrolling (unscrollable page, or page bottom = overscroll-to-close). The bottom `Collapse` footer becomes a **sticky liquid-glass pill** ("N Notifications ⌃", same `notifications-collapse` testid) that stays reachable while the inbox is in view. Outside-tap collapse and the directional no-toggle rule are unchanged.

Design exploration (4 interaction models compared with animated mockups + trade-off matrix) and the decision rationale: internal artifact `home-ux-lab` (linked in the tracking conversation).

## Evidence

- **Before/after screenshots (mobile 390×844 + desktop 1280×800)**: captured from the live `Shell/Home Dashboard` story with a seeded 9-notification mixed-priority inbox — before: apps gone + dead space; after: full inbox inline, app grid directly below, sticky pill during deep scroll. Attached inline below (first comment).
- **Real-browser e2e**: `bun run --cwd packages/ui test:home-screen-e2e` — **PASSED** (mobile touch expand/collapse, desktop pill flows, rail-swipe perf gate p95 9.8ms ≤ 33.3ms, 0 dropped frames, 0 page errors).

## Root cause

The original workflow first ran unrelated Bun script tests through the aggregate app test command. After that was corrected, exact-seed native verification exposed a second fault: the fixture contains both an embedded Home launcher and the dedicated launcher page, and the CDP driver selected the first matching tile. That tile was offscreen (`x=-371.75`), so the synthesized tap produced no launch telemetry. The settle check also included ambient descendant animations and unnecessarily exhausted its timeout.

# Deploy Notes

`staging-approval` was provisioned before merge while the original `staging` reviewer rule remains active, so there is no unprotected transition. After merge, remove required reviewers from `staging` while retaining its secrets and `develop` branch policy; reviewer policy remains on `staging-approval`.7d:T10dd,## Root cause

The active web chat renders the same assistant reply twice through two live transports:

1. The send path appends an optimistic `temp-resp-*` assistant bubble and `/api/conversations/:id/messages/stream` streams tokens into it.
2. The server persists the final assistant reply under a **different server UUID** and broadcasts it as a `proactive-message` WS frame (source `client_chat`) to the active conversation.
3. The proactive handler in `startup-phase-hydrate.ts` deduped **by id only**: same id → skip, otherwise append. Since the temp id and the persisted id never match, the echo appended as a second identical bubble.

Server-side persistence is NOT duplicated: the container-local transcript for the incident conversation had exactly one assistant row per user turn, and a staging-DB audit found zero adjacent duplicate persisted assistant rows. Full DB evidence in the fleet deliverable (`DOUBLE-MSG-2026-07-23.md`, sol lane; staging evidence log attached to the pr-evidence release for #17009).

## Fix: id reconciliation through the protocol (no text matching)

Replaces the rejected text-match suppression approach from #17009 (closed). Identity now flows end to end:

**Server**
- The terminal SSE `done` frame carries `messageId`, the durable persisted assistant memory id.
- The streaming success path pre-mints the id BEFORE emitting `done` and hands it to the deferred persist (`persistAssistantConversationMemory` gains an optional `memoryId`), so the done-before-persist latency optimization is untouched and the WS broadcast carries the same id.
- Action-callback turns that already persisted (and WS-echoed) mid-turn reuse that memory's id on `done` instead of minting a second one (`getRecentVisibleAssistantMemorySince` now returns `{ id, text }`).
- Wallet-guidance, streamed-then-failed, provider-failure, and idempotent-replay `done` frames all carry the persisted id too.

**Client**
- `streamChatEndpoint` surfaces `messageId` from the `done` frame.
- `useChatSend` passes it into the `complete` streaming modification as `persistedMessageId`; `useStreamingText` swaps the streamed `temp-resp-*` bubble to the persisted id **in place**, and collapses an already-appended WS echo bubble carrying that id.
- The `proactive-message` handler now reconciles by id: same id → update in place (or no-op when unchanged); different id → append. Genuinely new proactive messages still render.

## Tests

- `packages/agent/src/api/__tests__/conversation-stream-sse-contract.test.ts`: `done` frame carries `messageId` and the SAME id reaches the persistence layer (6/6 green).
- `packages/ui/src/state/__tests__/useStreamingText.test.ts`: id swap in place, echo-collapse on swap, id untouched without `persistedMessageId` (17/17 green).
- `packages/ui/src/state/startup-phase-hydrate.voice-control.test.ts`: echo with same persisted id reconciles instead of appending; distinct proactive messages still append (6/6 green).
- Also green: conversation-streaming (29), conversation/chat idempotency (20), failurekind roundtrip (10), useChatSend (74), client stream suites (23), startup-phase-hydrate suites (39).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean for all touched files in packages/agent + packages/ui; biome check clean on all touched files.

Part of the LifeOps MVP program — see packages/docs/ongoing-development/mvp/MVP.md (workstream 7).89:T580,Found during review of #16977.

Pool containers are provisioned under the sentinel `WARM_POOL_ORG_ID`, so `prepareManagedElizaBaseEnvironment` mints their `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY` (via `apiKeysService.createForAgent`) for the POOL org/user. `claimWarmContainer` transfers the DB row to the claiming user's org, and #16977 transfers the boot-coupled inbound auth keys — but the RUNNING container's outbound cloud identity (`ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY` in its process env) still belongs to the pool org until the next container restart re-materializes env from the row.

Consequences in the window between claim and first restart:
- cloud-API usage from the container (inference routing, usage tracking) attributes to the pool org, not the claiming org — billing/limits skew;
- revoking the claiming org's keys does not cut the container's cloud access, and vice versa.

Possible directions: mint the agent API key at claim time and include it in the post-claim push path (needs a container-side route to swap `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY` live), or rotate via a fast restart out-of-band after claim, or re-attribute pool-key usage rows at claim time. Needs design — the claim path's latency budget is the whole point of the warm pool.

Part of the LifeOps MVP program — see packages/docs/ongoing-development/mvp/MVP.md (workstream 6).8b:T1005,## Summary

Dedicated-agent provisioning is running the **cold path** in prod (~30–120s typical, up to ~11 min worst case) because the **warm pool is empty**: `WARM_POOL_ENABLED` is not set on the `eliza-provisioning-worker` daemon host, so `WarmPoolManager.replenish()` early-returns a no-op and the pool never refills. The replenish **wiring** was already fixed and deployed (#15310 / `b17fbbc7048`, in prod since the 2026-07-13 promote) — this is the remaining **config half**.

cc @0xSolace — your warm-pool lane (you authored the replenish fix). Diagnosed via read-only prod inspection (daemon journal + DB). **Zero code needed — two config settings.**

## Verified evidence

- `warmPoolEnabled()` defaults **false** — `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/config/containers-env.ts:647-651` (`raw === "true" || raw === "1"`).
- `WARM_POOL_ENABLED` is set truthy **nowhere in the repo or deploy config** — not in `wrangler.toml` `[vars]`/`[env.staging.vars]`/`[env.production.vars]`, not in any workflow. Read/tested only.
- On the provisioning-worker daemon host it is **absent from the daemon EnvironmentFile** (grep = 0, incl. the two most recent backups) → `replenish()` is a silent no-op (`agent-warm-pool.ts` → `"WARM_POOL_ENABLED=false (no-op)"`), and the log line is gated on `created>0||failed>0`, so nothing surfaces.
- **Prod DB: zero warm-pool rows** (`agent_sandboxes` has no `pool_status` entries). The Worker-side claim (`.../provision/route.ts:172`) therefore returns null and cold-paths regardless.
- The break is confessed in-code at `packages/scripts/cloud/admin/daemons/provisioning-worker.ts:1038-1046` ("THIS IS THE MISSING CALLER…"). The wiring fix `b17fbbc7048` is deployed; the enable flag most plausibly lived only in the retired control-plane sidecar's env and was never carried onto the daemon host.

## Fix — two settings, both required (A fills, B claims)

**A) Daemon (fills the pool):** set `WARM_POOL_ENABLED=true` in the provisioning-worker daemon's EnvironmentFile + restart → `processPoolReplenishCycle` (`provisioning-worker.ts:1730-1747`) fills within one infra-maintenance cycle (burst-limited to 3/cycle). Add the key to the daemon deploy workflow's env reconcile list so a control-plane re-arm can't silently drop it again (the #15160 drift class).

**B) Worker (claims at provision time):** add `WARM_POOL_ENABLED = "true"` as a **committed var** in `wrangler.toml [env.production.vars]` + deploy — **committed, not a dashboard secret** (`wrangler.toml:533-538` documents dashboard secrets getting wiped on Worker redeploys, which already silently re-closed apps-deploy once and is the likely cause of the original disappearance).

Either half alone leaves provisioning cold.

## Adjacent follow-ups (not the pool fix)

- The provisioning-worker daemon OOM-restarts under a 1024MB heap cap (frequent `Reached heap limit` fatals, clustered in ~6-hourly storms). Separate reliability issue — raise the heap and persist the mitigation out of ephemeral `/run/systemd`. It can intermittently trip the fail-closed heartbeat check and 503 creates, but it is **not** why the pool is empty (cycles complete between restarts and still create nothing with the flag off).
- `WarmPoolManager.healthCheck()` and `rollout()` have **no live caller** anywhere — stuck (10-min) and stale-image pool entries are never reaped. Consider wiring `healthCheck()` into a daemon phase.

## Ownership / suggested sequence

Half A is a prod ops action (env + restart; money surface — worth a sizing nod on how many warm containers to hold). Half B is a Worker PR + promote (your lane; carries the dashboard-secret-wipe redeploy risk). Suggested order: **A** (verify the pool fills via journal `warm pool replenish cycle complete` + DB `pool_status` rows) → **B** → confirm a test dedicated create claims warm (seconds instead of minutes).

Happy to do Half A and open the Half-B `wrangler.toml` PR if you want it off your plate — your call on the lane.

Make ordinary app-chat trajectories record the decisions needed to diagnose routing, context, and false-success failures.

- whether the final reply had a matching mutation receipt.

Scenario-runner file trajectories have richer stage data; bring the real app/database trajectory path up to the same diagnostic standard without leaking secrets or unbounded private context.

Record structured stages for message handling, retrieval, planning, tool/action calls and results, evaluation/final reply, and effect receipts. Include model/provider identity, latency/token usage, context/provider attribution hashes, candidate/retrieval scores, and redaction metadata. - native JSONL/export/redaction tests
- scenario/app parity tests

## Scope

The canonical **runtime** version covers package-manager declarations and Bun setup used to build, test, package, or release this repository. Bun type packages are supporting compatibility signals, not runtime selectors; the root type anchors must align, while historical workspace type ranges should be inventoried and changed only where they claim the repository runtime baseline.

A purpose-built upstream Bun compatibility matrix may add `canary` only as a non-authoritative extra cell with an explicit allowlist. It may not be the default, sole, required, frozen-install, build, deploy, or release runtime. Embedded Android/RISC-V Bun binary artifacts are a separate shipping boundary and require artifact/device proof rather than a blind text replacement.

96:T5f0,Found via hand-review of live-scenarios run 30046774252 (PR #17108 view-chat shard, scenario `live-document-delete`, native.jsonl planner row 2).

The planner injected a spurious `query:"list all"` into `DOCUMENT {action:"list"}`. In `packages/core/src/features/documents/actions.ts` (`handleList`, ~805–818) → `packages/core/src/features/documents/service.ts` (`listDocuments`, ~383), any planner-supplied `query` becomes a literal lowercase substring filter over content/title/filename, and zero matches renders the absolute statement **"No documents are available."** — conflating "no documents matched your filter" with "storage is empty". Downstream turns then rationally act on the poisoned result (the live scenario's turn 4 denied an existing document's existence).

This is the "empty must not impersonate not-found" doctrine violation: a filtered-empty result must be distinguishable from an empty store.

Fix in `handleList`: when `params.query` is non-empty and the filtered result is empty, return `No documents matched "<query>". <N> document(s) exist; retry without a query to list all.` — or auto-fallback to the unfiltered list with a no-matches-for-query preamble. Add a regression test covering query-miss vs truly-empty store.

Context: the same live-flake pattern (gpt-5-mini one-shot nondeterminism on byte-identical prompts) also exposed the settings-routing brittleness fixed in #17108's scenario wording; both flakes were triggers, but each uncovered a distinct real product brittleness.97:T62f,Every scheduled Live Scenarios run from 2026-07-12 through 2026-07-23 (12 consecutive nights) was cancelled at ~120 minutes, annotated 'The run was canceled forcefully by @github-actions[bot]'. The enforcing nightly live lane has not actually completed in that entire window — the 07-23 nightly finished all setup/build and died mid 'Run EA + connector live scenarios'.

Root cause (two independent ceilings, both too low):
1. `.github/workflows/actions-zombie-janitor.yml` force-cancels any in_progress run older than its default 120-minute max-age, and Live Scenarios is not in `ACTIONS_JANITOR_EXEMPT_WORKFLOWS` (currently only Cuttlefish + OpenAgent E1).
2. The workflow's own `timeout-minutes: 120` would kill it moments later regardless.

The nightly runs all four shards serially in one job on `ubuntu-24.04` (Hetzner fleet offline); historically successful nightlies took ~10–11 hours, so a 120-minute ceiling can never fit. (Before 07-12 the nightlies failed fast in setup; #16044's 07-11 fix got them running long enough to hit the reaper.)

Fix options:
- Exempt Live Scenarios from the janitor (or raise its max-age for this workflow) AND raise the workflow `timeout-minutes` to fit the measured serial duration; or
- Split the nightly into parallel per-shard jobs — #17108's shard architecture (per-shard artifact contract + one terminal aggregate gate) is the natural vehicle, with per-shard timeouts sized to each shard.

a2:T23cc,# Relates to

Refs #16917.

This PR is one staged foundation for the umbrella issue; it does **not** close
the umbrella. Follow-up production gates are tracked in:

- #17093 — strongly consistent authorization revocation and immutable session identity
- #17094 — bounded Durable Object calls and real workerd integration coverage
- #17095 — backward-compatible accounting revisions and projections
- #17096 — staged route adoption, rollback, and live evidence

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

# Critical review outcome

The original implementation was not safe to merge. It treated positive
authorization values in eventually consistent KV as a revocation boundary,
used unbounded Durable Object calls on the request path, swallowed alarm
recovery failures, did not scope one recovery lookup by tenant, and described
mocked Durable Object tests as integration coverage.

This revision separates authorization from admission:

- `INFERENCE_AUTH_CACHE_ENABLED` is independent and defaults to `false` in
  every checked-in environment.
- With that flag off, populated positive KV entries are ignored and origin
  authorization remains authoritative.
- The exact rate/spend Durable Object admission and revisioned accounting
  foundations can soak without enabling unsafe cached authorization.
- Authorization caching must remain off until #17093 provides a strongly
  consistent revocation boundary and immutable Steward session identity.

This is therefore a staged architectural foundation, not approval to enable
the complete cache-only hot path in production.

# What changes

- Covers `/v1/chat`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`,
  `/v1/responses`, `/v1/embeddings`, shared-agent turns, and the internal
  voice-session Eliza LLM turn.
- Adds revisioned authorization, pricing, policy, and balance projections.
- Adds per-organization Durable Objects for exact rate limiting and monetary
  leases, dispatch marking, settlement, and alarm recovery.
- Adds revision-aware, idempotent accounting and anonymous-inference recovery.
- Bounds admission-gate rate, lease, release, settlement, and dispatch calls;
  stalled admission fails closed.
- Makes alarm recovery failures observable and rethrows an aggregate failure
  so Cloudflare retries the alarm.
- Scopes recovery app lookup by both app ID and organization ID.
- Runs the production Durable Object in Miniflare/workerd with real storage and
  proves concurrent $7 leases against a $10 balance admit exactly one request.
- Adds the required Durable Object and rate-limiter bindings (with
  `new_sqlite_classes` migrations) in the default, staging, and production
  environments. Relies on the existing staging/production `CACHE_KV`
  namespaces; no KV binding is added, and the top-level dev environment
  still has no `CACHE_KV`.

Direct STT, TTS, and voice-clone media/job endpoints remain outside scope.

# Risk and rollout

**Deploy ordering:** the hot-path snapshot read selects
`organizations.balance_revision`, so migrations 0177-0181 must apply before or
with the Worker deploy (the deploy workflow's migration step already runs
first — keep that ordering). `INFERENCE_BILLING_LEDGER` flips `""` -> `"db"`
in all environments in this PR: it takes effect on staging with the next
develop deploy (the intended soak) and on production only via a later
main deploy, which stays gated on the #17096 evidence.

**Large / money path.** This changes admission, reservation, crash recovery,
settlement, affiliate payout, and balance projection. Require cloud/billing
owner review.

The warm path has serial Durable Object operations before provider dispatch.
Each client operation is bounded by a 1.5 second abort timeout. The included
benchmark is in-process and does not claim deployed Cloudflare latency.

Do not enable cached authorization or broadly adopt the route path until the
dependent issues above are complete and staging supplies rollback, latency,
revocation, recovery, and accounting evidence.

# Post-rebase deep review (five-dimension) — addendum

A five-dimension adversarial review (DO money path, auth-cache safety,
revisioned accounting, route integration, test realness) was run against this
branch after the rebase; every post-rebase CI failure was root-caused, and the
following landed on the branch (see the review comment for the full report):

- Sub-ledger-unit creator movements are a designed `below_ledger_unit` outcome
  (consumer charge proceeds, nothing recorded, auditable) instead of failing
  the reservation; creator-movement replays are first-committed-wins on keyed
  dedupe with identity fields strictly validated and a committed-row
  direction cross-check.
- Balance snapshot reads moved to a typed repository seam; the fail-closed
  balance tests now run against real PGlite with the real 0177 trigger and
  real corrupt values (`'NaN'::numeric`, NULL) — no mocked seams.
- Dead money-path modules removed (`createDeferredAdmissionSettler`,
  `recoverInferenceChargeViaLedger`); the DB-ledger settle now returns the
  real settlement transaction id.
- Session-path IAC cache writes are gated on `INFERENCE_AUTH_CACHE_ENABLED`
  (matching the API-key path); shared-agent session scope-cache hits
  revalidate `is_active`/org identity/org active from the lifecycle-
  invalidated user cache; cache validators are mutually exclusive.
- Streaming `onFinish` with absent usage settles at the admitted estimate,
  never $0 for delivered output; `/v1/chat` gained the stream settlement
  backstop; the messages-route terminal enqueue is guarded.

## Known limitations (tracked follow-ups)

- Shared-runtime local failures thrown before `onProviderDispatch` settle
  conservatively at the estimate; propagating a "dispatch never reached" flag
  would make zero provable (#17094).
- Negative shared-agent scope entries serve cached 401/403/404 for up to the
  30 s base TTL; mutation-side invalidation would remove that window (#17093).
- `uncollectedDebtUsd` in the gate DO only grows (no repayment interplay), and
  a corrupt-invariant alarm throw can freeze recovery for that org's leases
  until manual intervention; both are availability-direction, not money-loss,
  and belong to #17094/#17095.
- Only the lease/lease race runs under real workerd; settle/dispatch/release/
  alarm and the AnonymousChatGate DO are covered by in-memory-storage unit
  suites (#17094).

## Summary

This is a cohesive interaction and visual-stability pass across the home notification shade, continuous chat sheet, startup/auth surfaces, and local development runtime.

- Gives the notification shade shared momentum physics, endpoint resistance, stable detents, coordinated card/count/control fades, clean stack expansion/collapse, desktop clear-all confirmation, and isolated chat-vs-home gestures.
- Makes notification boot/reconnect snapshots authoritative while preserving concurrent arrivals, and tags replayed WebSocket events so one-shot UI effects are not repeated.
- Reworks chat actions, inline editing, replies, playback state, timestamps, transcription, long-draft scrolling, search, upload, and pending attachments so controls stay scoped to the correct message without unintended row or sheet movement.
- Makes message-search jumps deterministic by revealing already-loaded history before fetching and routing the jump through the canonical message scroller; the target lands in view with a neutral white highlight.
- Keeps the startup logo/name static while only status text shimmers, hides desktop pager arrows on mobile, reuses canonical cloud/device login launch surfaces, and runs the local Vite server under Node so HTTP upgrade/WebSocket proxying remains connected.

## Root causes

Notification drag physics, settle state, opacity, mounting, and glass presentation were driven by partially independent transitions. Chat action/reply/transcription controls participated in message and composer layout. Search fetched before revealing bounded history while bottom-follow could override imperative scrolling. Snapshot/replay handling could conflate reconnect state with new arrivals. The pre-React startup lockup and mounted shell used different geometry, and Bun-hosted Vite did not reliably preserve proxy upgrades.

## User impact

Notification pulls and stacks now track, settle, expand, collapse, and clear as one coherent surface. Chat controls stay minimal and stable. Older search hits reliably scroll into view. Voice/transcription and attachment workflows no longer unexpectedly open or collapse the sheet. Startup/auth transitions no longer morph or fork into duplicate UI, and mobile keeps swipe navigation without desktop arrows.

## Problem

The canonical Cloud Android post-build audit passed release `.aab` artifacts straight to `aapt dump badging` / `aapt dump xmltree`. AAPT is APK-only, so every valid App Bundle failed with `no AndroidManifest.xml found` before any strip-policy assertion could run. There was no bundle-aware tooling anywhere in the repo.

## Fix

- **New `packages/app-core/scripts/lib/android-cloud-artifact-audit.mjs`** — bundle-aware audit built on Google's official bundletool **1.18.3**, pinned by SHA-256 (`a099cfa1…8e29`). The pin is enforced at provisioning (`ensureAndroidBundletoolJar`: env-configured JAR must match the digest; otherwise a one-time download into a content-verified cache, atomic rename, no unpinned fallback) and **re-verified immediately before every bundletool spawn** (TOCTOU defense). All bundletool invocations carry a 120 s timeout and surface child-process failures (spawn error, non-zero exit, signal, timeout) as typed `ElizaError`s.
- **`auditAndroidCloudArtifact` now branches on artifact kind** (`resolveAndroidArtifactKind`): APK auditing keeps the exact AAPT badging/xmltree + DEX behavior; AAB auditing runs `bundletool validate`, decodes **every module manifest** (`dump manifest --module=…`, base required, traversal-shaped module names rejected), and scans **every module's `dex/classes*.dex`**. Private LP3 actions, permissions, components, classes, and policy markers remain forbidden in ordinary Cloud/Play/AOSP artifacts — no strip or policy check was weakened; the AOSP/system audit additionally gained the manifest-marker + DEX-marker assertions.
- **Gradle wiring** (`platforms/android/app/build.gradle`): for `elizaCloudBuild` builds, an `auditCloudReleaseAab` finalizer resolves the exact release bundle via the AGP `SingleArtifact.BUNDLE` API and runs the audit-only CLI on it, fail-closed — a failed, skipped, or outcome-less `bundleRelease` is a hard error, never a silent skip. The orchestrator passes `process.execPath` through as `NODE_BINARY` so the finalizer works where `node` is not on Gradle's PATH.
- **New audit-only CLI target**: `node scripts/run-mobile-build.mjs android-cloud-audit [aab-path]`, and the audit emits a machine-readable attestation line (`[mobile-build] android-cloud AAB attestation {json}`) carrying the bundletool version and the artifact SHA-256/size.
- `scripts/lib/eliza-error.mjs` gives the build scripts a local `ElizaError` so they do not depend on `@elizaos/core`'s built dist.

## Tests

`packages/app-core/scripts/run-mobile-build-android-aab-audit.test.mjs` covers the acceptance matrix: valid clean AAB, forbidden manifest marker, forbidden DEX marker (including feature-module-only), malformed/truncated bundle, missing tool, child-process failure/signal/timeout, bundletool digest pinning (configured JAR, download, corrupt download), APK-path regression contract (exact AAPT commands preserved), boundary hardening, and the Gradle wiring contract. An opt-in real lane (`ELIZA_ANDROID_RUN_REAL_AAB_TEST=1`) runs real bundletool against the byte-pinned multi-module fixture from Google's bundletool repo (`test/fixtures/android/install-time-permanent-modules.aab`, Apache-2.0, SHA-256 documented in the fixture README).

ac:T2b68,Closes #16896.

## Why

This replaces the unsafe timeout/fallback proposed in #16882 and the mocked timing gate in #16820.

A generic `Promise.race` around prompt providers is not latency control. It returns apparently valid empty context, leaves the losing operation running, can cache the fabricated fallback, and hides the component that is actually broken. Reducing that race from 30 seconds to 3 seconds only makes the hidden failure happen sooner.

The runtime should execute independent work concurrently, reuse valid work maximally, cancel work only through a real `AbortSignal`, and report every stage precisely enough that a slow request names its cause.

## Runtime behavior

- Runs every selected prompt provider concurrently with `Promise.all`.
- Reuses all valid per-turn, stable, and max-cache provider results unless the caller explicitly refreshes a provider.
- Coalesces identical in-flight provider work for the same message/provider.
- Makes the planner's second composition max-cache and refreshes only `RECENT_MESSAGES` when the early reply changed it.
- Passes the owning request/stream `AbortSignal` through provider, document-recall, embedding, OpenAI, and ElizaCloud embedding paths.
- Throws and reports provider failures instead of manufacturing empty prompt context.
- Moves semantic document recall into the parallel `DOCUMENTS` provider; the serial pre-model augmentation is lexical only and warms clean-prompt embedding out of band.
- Makes available-app registry lookup stale-while-revalidate and prewarmed, and makes wallet prompt composition cache-only with a coalesced background refresh.
- Removes abandoned timeout races and fabricated `[]`/`null` results from orchestrator provider/database paths.
- Isolates model-usage capture per async request so concurrent turns on one runtime cannot contaminate each other's call or token totals.

## Full request telemetry

One `chat-request` flow now measures the complete path from request receipt through response finalization, with exclusive stage accounting for:

`document-augmentation`, `providers`, `embedding`, `model-queue`, `model-routing`, `model-preprocess`, `llm-inference`, `model-postprocess`, `actions`, `evaluators`, `planner-overhead`, `response-finalization`, `message-service-overhead`, and `unattributed`.

It also records first model token, first visible output, reply delivery, finalization, provider outcome/cache/coalescing, model provider/attempt/outcome, prompt/completion/total tokens, and prompt-cache read/creation tokens when the model SDK reports them. Summaries, histograms, provider outcomes, and flows are available from the development latency endpoint.

## Timeout policy

Removed:

- 30-second/3-second prompt-provider `Promise.race` fallback from #16882.
- 4-second document lookup race that did not cancel the lookup.
- 5-second recovery LLM call that hid a broken primary path.
- 2-second orchestrator provider/database races that returned fake empty values.

Retained only real cancellation or non-critical lifecycle boundaries:

- outer chat request: 180 seconds, aborts the owned request tree;
- ElizaCloud text generation: 120 seconds, aborts the HTTP request;
- embeddings: 60 seconds, aborts the HTTP request/backoff and cannot fall through after abort;
- wallet RPC: 4 seconds through viem transport cancellation;
- optional title generation: 5 seconds, outside reply correctness;
- post-delivery side effect: 30 seconds, detached and diagnostically reported.

These retained boundaries do not turn a failure into healthy-empty prompt state. A 30-second interactive response is still broken; telemetry now identifies the stage, while the outer boundary prevents leaked work.

## #16820 review and replacement

#16820 is a deterministic browser-test concept, not production latency telemetry: it mocks `fetch` and SSE, starts timing before the click, treats a DOM mutation as a paint, inserts a synthetic 35-second idle, and computes p95 from two samples.

The replacement Chromium test drives the real chat UI, starts at the click, observes React commits after `requestAnimationFrame`, requires at least three distinct assistant text lengths before completion, and proves incremental rendering rather than one final paint. It remains a deterministic client-render regression test and is not mislabeled as server/model latency.

Follow-up to #16925. The response-tail change in that PR was real, but ordinary Worker chat requests could still hit Postgres before model dispatch for authentication, billing admission, agent resolution, conversation history, and voice scope checks.

## What changed

- Makes the ordinary user/organization Worker inference path cache-only before model dispatch.
- Treats cold cache entries as a short `503` warming state and schedules authoritative hydration with `waitUntil`; stale entries are served immediately and refreshed asynchronously.
- Adds a per-agent/per-room `SharedRuntimeConversation` Durable Object. Durable Object storage is the ordered, authoritative live conversation state; legacy history migration and Postgres mirrors run off the response path.
- Defers shared-tier billing admission/accounting and linked-character hydration without allowing an uncached database fallback into the LLM hot path.
- Applies the same cache-only contract to REST chat, SSE chat, OpenAI-compatible chat completions, Anthropic-compatible messages, the agent bridge, and voice scope resolution.
- Preserves synchronous reservation-coupled semantics for explicit affiliate/app-monetization and non-Worker fallback paths.
- Registers sliding cache refreshes with the Worker execution context so refresh work is observable and allowed to finish.

## CI coverage policy

- Removes the 50% per-file changed-source coverage floor.
- Removes the shared Vitest 25/25/25/15 global percentage floors.
- Removes app-core surface percentage thresholds and threshold-only reporting.
- Removes zero-valued CLI threshold overrides and stale threshold recommendations.
- Keeps the useful non-percentage guarantees: changed executable source must appear in LCOV, it cannot have zero executable lines, and changed production code still requires changed tests.
- Correctly excludes `.d.ts`, `.d.mts`, and `.d.cts` declarations from changed executable-source classification.
